lifecycles._note: Light governance lifecycle for loggingaudit (audit trails / CloudTrail-equivalent). Covers all 6 uncovered writes: createtrail(POST /v1/trails), settrail(PUT /v1/trails/{trail_id}), starttrail(POST /v1/trails/{trail_id}/start), stoptrail(POST /v1/trails/{trail_id}/stop), deletetrail(DELETE /v1/trails/{trail_id}), downloadlogs(POST /v1/logs/download). Body validated 2026-06-20 against TrailCreateRequestV1dot1 schema (data/api_docs.json key management/loggingaudit/trailcreaterequestv1dot1): required fields are account_id, bucket_name, bucket_region, trail_name, trail_save_type. A capture-account-id pre-step (GET /v1/access-keys via iam service) soft-captures the caller's account_id before createtrail fires. createtrail typically requires a real object-storage bucket to receive logs, so a 400/403/422 is still expected on the shared account; every mutating step is optional with a broad expect_status so it RECORDS coverage without failing. trail_id capture path $.trail.id confirmed by response_example. start/stop are POSTs without a body. downloadlogs is a coverage-only POST (it may stream a file on success; we only assert it is reachable). DELETE is destructive (gated).

steps.name: capture-account-id
steps._note: Cross-service pre-step (iam host, read-only). Soft-captures caller's account_id from the IAM access-key list ($.access_keys[0].account_id) — the same pattern as iam-readonly-shows lifecycle (management__iam.json line 580). account_id is REQUIRED by createtrail schema (TrailCreateRequestV1dot1, api_docs.json) — the 400 ValidationError 'Field required' in the prior light run was caused by its absence. If the list returns empty or 403, account_id stays a literal {account_id} placeholder; createtrail will still 400 (no worse than before) while remaining callable.

steps.name: create-trail
steps._note: Body fixed 2026-06-20: (1) added account_id (REQUIRED per TrailCreateRequestV1dot1 schema in api_docs.json — was causing 400 ValidationError 'Field required'); captured from iam capture-account-id pre-step. (2) changed log_type_total_yn N->Y for consistency (when N, target_log_types must be non-empty per API semantics; Y with empty array is safe). (3) replaced tags->tag_create_requests (correct field name per schema; 'tags' is not a valid TrailCreateRequest field). Source: data/api_docs.json key management/loggingaudit/trailcreaterequestv1dot1 (required fields: account_id, bucket_name, bucket_region, trail_name, trail_save_type). Response envelope $.trail.id confirmed by response_example. bucket_name FIXED 2026-07-16 (new test account post 2026-07-15 cutover): do-not-delete-apitest no longer exists in this account (head_bucket 404, confirmed live). The pre-existing fixture bucket apitest-logsink (core.oplog.LOGSINK_BUCKET, plain private bucket in the CURRENT test account, confirmed live via list_buckets 2026-07-16) is the correct target — same bucket network-logging storages use. bucket_region={region} resolves to SCP_REGION (kr-west1), matching the bucket's actual object-store host region; doc's 'RegionOne' example is a generic placeholder, not a real enum. service_watch_yn FIXED 2026-07-16 Y->N: live 400 'invalid service watch values' when service_watch_yn=Y without iam_role_id+log_group_name (doc's own request_example sets both when service_watch_yn=Y — description says those two fields are 'Service Watch 트레일에만 해당' i.e. only meaningful/required together with it). N (plain trail, no Service Watch / CloudWatch-equivalent integration) needs neither and is the minimal-viable create.

steps.name: set-trail
steps._note: Body from api_docs.json settrail request_example (2026-06-20). No bucket_name/bucket_region on update (immutable). Fields match the PUT schema: trail_description, trail_save_type, and all yn-flag arrays. log_type_total_yn changed N->Y (consistent with createtrail fix: when N the API may require non-empty target_log_types). service_watch_yn FIXED 2026-07-16 Y->N (same 'invalid service watch values' 400 as createtrail — Y requires iam_role_id+log_group_name, which this minimal update body doesn't set).

steps.name: delete-trail
steps._note: If create captured no id, {trail_id} stays literal and the DELETE normalizes to the catalog '*' key (records coverage) and 404s harmlessly.

steps.name: download-logs
steps._note: Coverage POST. Body CORRECTED 2026-06-20 from api_docs.json LogDownloadRequest schema (required: start_at, end_at, file_type, time_zone_info — NOT trail_id/start_dt/end_dt which were wrong). file_type=CSV (or JSON; API accepts both). time_zone_info=UTC. Isolated group so a 4xx never affects the trail group. No trail_id required — this downloads raw activity logs, not trail-archived data.

lifecycles._note: Light, READ-ONLY (no writes, no cleanup). Closes the static id-bound GET gap GET /v1/logs/{logging_id} (showlog) by the list->soft-capture->show idiom. LIVE-CONFIRMED 2026-06-20: listlogs with start_at=2025-01-01T00:00:00Z & end_at=2026-12-31T23:59:59Z returns 200 (count=70444+, the account has extensive activity log history). showlog with real log id returns 200. Envelope: LogListResponse{count, logs:[Log], page, size, sort}; Log.id is the correct field. IMPORTANT: data/api_catalog_params.json showlog capture path is WRONG ($.contents[0].id — no 'contents' field in response); correct path is $.logs[0].id as coded here. The trail lifecycle never satisfies showlog (different resource type). listlogs REQUIRES start_at + end_at (ISO-8601 UTC per constraint listlogs-needs-time-window). Wide static window 2025-01-01..2026-12-31 maximises hit. {today} builtin is %Y%m%d NOT ISO-8601 — do NOT use it here. Both steps optional [200,400,403,404].

steps.name: list-logs
steps._note: listlogs with the REQUIRED start_at + end_at time window (ISO-8601 UTC) sent via params (service constraint listlogs-needs-time-window). A wide static window maximises the chance the account has at least one activity log to soft-capture ($.logs[0].id, LogListResponse.logs[].id). Tolerant [200,400,403,404]: empty/denied/missing-window all still let the show below be CALLED.

steps.name: show-log
steps._note: id-bound read (showlog). Closes GAP-get-id for GET /v1/logs/{logging_id}. Keys off the list-captured logging_id (a real id when the window has any logs -> 2xx); if the window is empty the segment stays a placeholder (normalizes to catalog '*') and 4xx's. Tolerant [200,400,403,404]; the GET is CALLED so the endpoint is statically reachable.
